note: Trimmed from Rubato Audio's Plaits Palette catalog (lylepmills/eurorack, alt_firmwares/plaits_lab_catalog).

engines.name: Virtual Analog
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Continuously variable analog waveforms with detuning and sync.

engines.name: Virtual Analog Dual
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: One of Emilie Gillet's alternate virtual-analog designs preserved in the Plaits source: independent waveforms, interval detuning, and a synchronized alternate output.

engines.name: Virtual Analog Crossfade
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: One of Emilie Gillet's alternate virtual-analog designs preserved in the Plaits source: a waveform pair crossfading from detune through dry tone to hard sync.

engines.name: Waveshaping
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A variable waveshaper for clean sines, folded tones, and hard edges.

engines.name: Two-op FM
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A focused two-operator FM voice spanning pure bells to metallic noise.

engines.name: Granular Formant
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Granular formants and filtered noise animated around the fundamental.

engines.name: Harmonic Oscillator
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A bank of additive partials with spectral balance and timbral motion.

engines.name: Wavetable
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Smooth travel through an extensive collection of integrated waves.

engines.name: Chords
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Four-voice chord voicings with selectable waveforms and inversions.

engines.name: Speech
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Vowels, phonemes, speech synthesis, and word banks in one voice.

engines.name: Speech Sounds
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A split of Emilie Gillet's Speech model in the Plaits source: Naive, SAM, and LPC phonemes spread continuously across one playable model.

engines.name: LPC Words
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A split of Emilie Gillet's Speech model in the Plaits source: LPC word banks with selected stock or custom banks, direct speed, and recorded prosody.

engines.name: Swarm
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A cloud of detuned sawtooth oscillators for supersaws and drones.

engines.name: Filtered Noise
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Clocked noise and multimode filtering for pitched or diffuse spectra.

engines.name: Particle Noise
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Random particles excite a resonant network from sparse ticks to clouds.

engines.name: Inharmonic String
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A physical string model moving from clean plucks to inharmonic material.

engines.name: Modal Resonator
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Modal synthesis for strings, plates, tubes, bells, and struck objects.

engines.name: Analog Bass Drum
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A punchy synthesized kick with controllable tone, decay, and drive.

engines.name: Analog Snare
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A modeled snare combining tuned oscillators and filtered noise.

engines.name: Analog Hi-hat
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Metallic cymbal oscillators and noise shaped into crisp hi-hats.

engines.name: VA + VCF
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Classic oscillator shapes through a resonant virtual-analog filter.

engines.name: Phase Distortion
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Casio-inspired phase distortion with animated harmonic contours.

engines.name: 6-Op FM Bank A
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: The first bank of classic DX7-compatible six-operator FM patches stored in Plaits user data.

engines.name: 6-Op FM Bank B
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: The second bank of classic DX7-compatible six-operator FM patches stored in Plaits user data.

engines.name: 6-Op FM Bank C
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: The third bank of classic DX7-compatible six-operator FM patches stored in Plaits user data.

engines.name: Wave Terrain
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Two-dimensional navigation across a continuously changing terrain.

engines.name: String Machine
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Divide-down ensemble strings with chord voicings and lush animation.

engines.name: Chiptune
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Three square-wave voices with arpeggiation and game-console grit.

engines.name: Natural Speech
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Spoken words resynthesized through a vocal tract you can reshape, from mumbled to over-enunciated.

engines.name: Glisson
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Overlapping grains trace randomized upward and downward pitch glides.

engines.name: GENDY
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: A waveform continuously rewritten by amplitude and duration random walks.

engines.name: Scanned
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Scan across a slowly evolving network of coupled virtual masses.

engines.name: Pulsar
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Windowed tone bursts move from sparse impulses to clustered formant rhythms.

engines.name: Loopback
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: A normalized feedback-AM loop creates recursive sidebands without running away.

engines.name: Lockstep
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: An audible internal phase-locked loop hunts, slips, and captures harmonic ratios.

engines.name: Tapfield
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Pitch-clocked Galois feedback registers become repeating binary wavefields.

engines.name: Phase Weave
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Four asymmetric harmonic voices weave through moving cancellation geometries.

engines.name: Sideband Bank
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Finite discrete-summation banks build compact geometric ladders above and below a carrier.

engines.name: Attractor
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: A bounded three-state cyclic flow turns deterministic attractor motion into audio.

engines.name: Undertow
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Six integer undertones blend through original registrations and a warped divider lattice.

engines.name: Reed Pipe
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: A nonlinear reed excites a fractional-delay bore with a movable pressure pickup.

engines.name: Phase Flock
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Seven mean-field phase oscillators disperse, synchronize, and split into antipodal clusters.

engines.name: Rulefield
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Elementary cellular-automaton generations become evolving 32-cell wavecycles.

engines.name: Spectral Spiral
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: A complex delay loop repeatedly frequency-shifts an analytic harmonic source.

engines.name: Z Filter
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' four filter models in one slot: a windowed resonator burst rung against a polarity-flipped pulse train and its integral.

engines.name: Toy
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A bit-mangled phase ramp read through a sample-and-hold clock that can free-run or lock to the played note.

engines.name: CSaw
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: The emblematic Braids sawtooth, with a notch cut into the start of every cycle and a bendable ramp.

engines.name: Ring Mod
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A carrier ring-modulated by two independently detuned sines, driven through a saturating shaper.

engines.name: Fold
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' two wavefolders crossfaded against each other, the sine one saturating where the triangle one keeps folding. The model Plaits' Waveshaping model descends from, with the second curve it left behind.

engines.name: Buzz
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' two unison-tuned band-limited pulse trains, summed. Harmonic count comes from a wavetable zone lookup, not a live additive sum, so the sweep is a flat spectrum with a hard cutoff moving through it, not a shaped one.

engines.name: Dual Sync
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' two hard-sync models in one engine: a master oscillator syncs a slave swept up to 64 semitones above it, crossfaded against it. Virtual Analog's sync square shares one knob with pulse width and gain, and has no balance.

engines.name: Granular Cloud
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' asynchronous grain cloud: four windowed sine grains respawning on a coin flip, each taking a fresh random pitch. Where Granular Formant stays locked to a carrier, this one scatters until the pitch is gone.

engines.name: Morph
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' one-knob walk from triangle through saw to a narrowing pulse, into a low-pass that tracks the note and a tanh fuzz. Virtual Analog shares the waveforms and has neither.

engines.name: Noise Bank
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' three noise models in one slot: noise through a resonant filter, two resonant peaks, and a sample-and-hold whose random sequence loops into a pitched buzz.

engines.name: Particle Burst
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' PRTC: three fixed-interval resonant filters, a chord above the note, re-struck by a shared decaying noise burst at a random rate. Plaits' Particle Noise scatters six particles around one pitch instead — a cloud, not a chord.

engines.name: Saw Square
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' variable saw and variable square, driven from one shared TIMBRE knob that opens one as it closes the other, crossfaded by COLOR. Virtual Analog runs the same pair of waveforms independently; this is the coupled, single-knob version.

engines.name: Saw Swarm
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' seven-voice detuned sawtooth chorus, soft-clipped and carved by a resonant filter tracking the note. A fixed chorus of deliberately raw, aliasing sawtooths — not the granular cloud of Plaits' own Swarm model.

engines.name: Vowel
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' table-driven vowel synthesizer: three formants read at sixteen steps a cycle, gated by a ramp that restarts every pitch period, through a tanh shaper. The stepped ancestor of Speech's SAM mode.

engines.name: Harmonics
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' twelve-partial additive stack, with two Lorentzian bumps sliding over the harmonic series. Its integer amplitude slew gates quiet partials out entirely, the grain the Plaits Harmonic Oscillator's float smoothing does not have.

engines.name: VOSIM
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' VOSM: two sine formants under a bell window the played note restarts. Both formant pitches are absolute and set independently, reaching pairs Granular Formant's ratio control cannot, and the 2:1 balance is a knob.

engines.name: Plucked
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' PLUK: three round-robin Karplus-Strong voices, a noise burst dropped into a resonant loop per strike. Inharmonic String is the same round robin with a far more elaborate model; this keeps PLUK's own stochastic damping instead.

engines.name: Blown
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' blown bore: one delay line closed by an inverting reflection, driven by a clipped reed and a breath pressure the noise rides on. Its tone filter sits outside the loop, so the body color and the pipe are separate controls.

engines.name: Struck Bell
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' BELL: eleven fixed inharmonic partials, additively synthesized and struck once per trigger, sharing one decay curve and one odd/even detune. A fixed hand-tuned voicing, not a stretched-harmonic formula.

engines.name: Struck Drum
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' DRUM: six fixed partials struck once per trigger. Two are ring-modulated by lowpass-filtered noise instead of played straight — a different mechanism from a resonator excited by noise.

engines.name: Kick
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' self-enveloping kick: two decaying pulses into a bandpass that jumps up in pitch for a brief click, then self-brightens. A different mechanism from Plaits' own Analog Bass Drum, which clicks with FM rather than a retuned filter.

engines.name: Snare
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' SNAR: two decaying pulses into two fixed-interval tonal resonators, and a decaying noise burst into a third, high resonator, all self-enveloping and summed. A note strikes shorter the higher it is played.

engines.name: Cymbal
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' CYMBAL: six square oscillators through a resonant bandpass, crossfaded against clocked noise through a resonant highpass. Free-running, not self-enveloping.

engines.name: Wave Scan
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' three wavetable models in one slot, over its own set of 256 8-bit waves: 20 named banks, a 16x16 interpolated map, and a curated line with a phase-domain crush.

engines.name: Wave Paraphonic
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Four wavetable voices play the active Plaits chord table over Braids' 33-wave scan line, with per-voice wave fan and continuous interval scaling.

engines.name: Fluted
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A jet flute derived from Braids' FLUT: a bore and a jet delay line sharing one loop, driven by an asymmetric cubic jet and a breath the noise multiplies. It overblows into a higher register, as the module does.

engines.name: Question Mark
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' hidden model, reachable on the module only with the marquee set to “49”: a Morse transmitter keying a sine over a drifting noise bed, through a squared-distortion stage.

engines.name: Virtual Analog Variant
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Emilie Gillet's two alternate virtual-analog designs preserved in the Plaits source, unified: a detuned or hard-synced second oscillator on one trajectory, with independently spread waveshapes.

engines.name: Bowed
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A bowed string waveguide with a stick-slip friction exciter, a movable bow, and an adjustable instrument body.

engines.name: Sub Osc
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A shaped main oscillator against a square sub one or two octaves down, loudest at both ends of the sub control.

engines.name: Digital Modulation
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A carrier driven by a framed packet of dibits through a four-point constellation, with an openable frame.

engines.name: Saw Comb
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: A band-limited exciter through a comb whose pitch is decoupled from the played note, with genuinely bipolar feedback.

engines.name: Vowel FOF
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Five very narrow filters sweeping five vowels across five vocal registers, with the formant balance Braids leaves flat. The ancestor of Speech's naive mode, on the same vowel and register grid, carried here at finer resolution.

engines.name: Raw FM
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Braids' three FM models on one axis: self-feedback, plain two-operator FM, and chaotic frequency feedback. The ancestor of Two-op FM, sharing its ratio quantizer and feedback axis, run raw: unfiltered feedback, no oversampling.

engines.name: Triple
engines.author: Emilie Gillet
engines.description: Three oscillators with two continuously swept interval knobs, morphing together through square, saw, triangle, and sine. It overlaps Chords and Swarm in territory, not lineage: intervals you sweep rather than a table you author.

engines.name: Bytebeat
engines.author: Tim Churches
engines.description: Four integer expressions read as audio, pitch-tracked and with an openable mask width. From Tim Churches' Bees-in-the-Trees firmware for Braids.

engines.name: Diatonic Chord
engines.author: Tom Burns
engines.description: Chords stacked in scale degrees rather than fixed intervals, so the quality follows the played note. From Tom Burns' Braids Renaissance firmware.

engines.name: Scale Stack
engines.author: Tom Burns
engines.description: Five voices spaced an equal number of scale degrees apart, sweeping from cluster to wide chord without ever leaving the scale. From Tom Burns' Braids Renaissance firmware.

engines.name: Wavetable Diatonic Chord
engines.author: Tom Burns
engines.description: Diatonic chords over Braids Renaissance's WTCH scan, with independent voice spread and wavetable position. From Tom Burns' Braids Renaissance firmware.

engines.name: Wavetable Scale Stack
engines.author: Tom Burns
engines.description: Five scale-spaced voices over Braids Renaissance's WTx6 scan, with independent span, spread, and wavetable position. From Tom Burns' Braids Renaissance firmware.

engines.name: Shakers
engines.author: Lyle Mills, after Perry R. Cook and Gary P. Scavone
engines.description: Sixteen shaken and scraped instruments from Perry Cook's PhISEM, which models the statistics of colliding objects rather than any one object's shape.

engines.name: Brass
engines.author: Lyle Mills, after Perry R. Cook and Gary P. Scavone
engines.description: A lip-reed brass instrument after Perry R. Cook and Gary P. Scavone's STK brass model. Breath makes it speak, and the lip knob climbs the bore's harmonic series the way a bugle player does.

engines.name: Helix
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: A chord stacked across octaves on a Shepard helix, gliding endlessly up or down without ever changing register.

engines.name: Skins
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Struck membrane modes move from a round open head to a tighter loaded skin, with center, rim, damping, and pitch-dive control.

engines.name: Circuit Zaps
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Falling-pitch electronic strikes cross two oscillators into ring-modulated zaps, sparks, and driven discharges.

engines.name: Metalwork
engines.author: Lyle Mills
engines.description: Paired inharmonic modes turn one struck-metal model into anvil, agogo, plate, and gong families with controllable beating.

engines.name: Analog Clap
engines.author: Dylan Bolink
engines.description: 808-style clap, noise gated a few milliseconds at a time into a wide band with a steep bottom, and a longer tail for the room. Four hands become seven that disagree; unpatched, an audience.

engines.name: Analog Percussion
engines.author: Dylan Bolink
engines.description: The 808's tuned percussion: toms, congas, rimshot, claves, and cowbell are points in one plane of pitch, ring length, and material rather than separate instruments.

engines.name: Freshets Formant
engines.author: Dylan Bolink
engines.description: A driver oscillator firing a Serge-style AD envelope read through a waveshaper. Pulses arriving mid-attack are skipped, so low ratios subdivide the driver instead of retriggering it. Ported from Tides 2 Freshets alternative firmware.

engines.name: BubbleTime
engines.author: Combust
engines.description: A bubbly point-process instrument: strike timing drawn from a rigidity ladder (hyperuniform to clustered) pings chord-tone plucks. A bubbling timing generator at CV rates; a bubbling arp at audio rates.

engines.name: ZxPhase48k
engines.author: Combust
engines.description: ZX Spectrum beeper interference synthesis: two squares boolean-combined on a 1-bit bus that also XORs with its own past — a boolean flanger. Audio into V/OCT is crushed block-rate FM, on purpose.

engines.name: ZxPulse48k
engines.author: Combust
engines.description: Follin-style 1-bit pulse-frequency modulation: chord-bank driven pin-train stacks and arpeggios with pulse-width-as-volume, tick-quantized echo, load-dependent pitch pull, and selectable voice-level stereo.

engines.name: Acid
engines.author: Dylan Bolink
engines.description: A silver-box bassline voice: one saw-to-pulse oscillator into a four-pole ladder, then a diode-style clipper. The filter sweep is DECAY through MORPH's attenuverter, and LEVEL is a real accent.

engines.name: Supersaw Chords
engines.author: Dirk Hoppmann
engines.description: Chords on unevenly detuned saw stacks, with a saturator on TIMBRE and the detune spread on MORPH.
